paper.title: UniIntervene: Agentic Intervention for Efficient Real-World Reinforcement Learning
paper.central_claim: Future-conditioned value estimation, temporal stagnation risk and memory-goal-conditioned autonomous recovery internalize interventions in real-world HiL-RL, improving average manipulation success by8.6% while reducing human interventions by57% relative to state-of-the-art HiL baselines.

signatures.object: Recovery memory and goal-conditioned action policy
signatures.information: Recorded RGB/state failure/start and future goal pairs; per-task memory selected by instruction; normalized embedding cosine retrieval. State modality details less explicit than main observation definition.
signatures.operation: Mine fixed-span proxy-improving segments; progress-bin quota and per-episode cap; retrieve top1 goal; FAST-tokenized BC decoder produces8-step action chunk; add real transitions to replay.
signatures.conditions: Memory contains relevant reachable goals and policy can reach them from off-memory learner states. High proxy value alone does not verify physical recovery.
signatures.feedback: Proxy value lift and eventual observed task outcome; fallback human remains.
signatures.selection_rule: Threshold on future proxy value, start reasonably high, minimum rise.4/.5; retain120/task or240 towel; top cosine goal.
signatures.selection_data: Candidate pools~3k–40k existing segments; training-rollout retrieval audit only.
signatures.persistence: Static per-task memory and BC recovery parameters; replay buffer supports later learner updates.
signatures.later_use: Autonomous intervention within online RL and residual human unsafe/OOD takeover.
signatures.claimed_effect: Restore productive exploration with fewer human corrections.
signatures.failure_boundary: Unknown failure modes, no-match/unsafe retrieval rejection, repeated takeover/hysteresis and explicit goal-completion handback not fully specified. No demonstrated held-out task-memory transfer.

gap.author_gap: HiL-RL reuses human corrections but still requires human-triggered rescue from rollouts that are safe yet unproductive; safety/reset criteria miss progress stagnation.
gap.checked_gap: Concrete distinction between safety/failure and progress monitoring, with intervention-rate baseline and ablations on contact-rich tasks. Broad assertion that stagnation dominates human labor is not directly measured by a human-cost taxonomy.

lineage/closest_adjacent.relation: HIL-SERL corrective off-policy RL; failure-aware recovery (FA-RL); reset-free/reversible policies and safety critics.
lineage/closest_adjacent.scope: Author descriptions and local implementation summary only; original nearest-neighbor texts not present.

gap.residue: Learn when ongoing rollout is losing value and where/how to recover without human corrections for each stall.
gap.stakes: Physical RL data collection and human operator burden, not merely offline failure classifier accuracy.
gap.method_response: Future-value prediction stabilizes monitor; temporal trends reject transient dips; past high-value goals resolve recovery target; learned correction feeds replay.
gap.remaining_gap: Proxy/time labels may encode duration/outcome rather than causal progress; memory coverage/heldout retrieval not validated; training budget, attention time and safety events absent; control handback/normalization ambiguity.

claims.text: Autonomous value-aware intervention improves real-world success while reducing human correction burden.
claims.setting: UR7e5 manipulation tasks, randomized initial poses;20 evaluations/task after training;IR3 independent training runs.
claims.baseline/control: pi0.5 SFT20 demos/task, HiL-SERL, HiL-SERL+FA-RL; same hardware/cameras/SpaceMouse.
claims.selection_vs_test: Proxy/intervention/recovery trained from scored past rollouts, per-task memory; test episodes after training but full episode/data budget separation not documented.
claims.result/denominator: MeanSR81→88 is+7 percentage points or8.64% relative; IR34.3→14.6 is−19.7pp/57.4% relative. SR20/task, IR intervention steps/robot steps, not takeover-event count or human hours.
counterevidence: SR uncertainty and per-run IR variance not reported;20 episodes/task means5pp resolution.
Total robot/compute/offline-data and operator-time budgets not matched. Reset/oversight labor excluded from IR.
Unclear whether posttraining evaluations use recovery and/or residual humans; cannot assign all outcome gain to learned base policy.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Author-reported higher final task success and lower human intervention-step fraction on these trained real tasks; not proof of general labor saving, safety, cross-domain transfer or autonomous learner improvement absent stack.

claims.text: Future value/temporal risk detect stagnation and memory-guided recovery restores productive progress.
claims.setting: Offline proxy/trigger metrics and two-task component ablations; qualitative successful RAM/towel episodes.
claims.baseline/control: Without future prediction, value prediction, temporal value-risk, memory goal.
claims.selection_vs_test: Proxy held-out episode validation reported; memory retrieval audit training queries; mined trigger labels use same proxy rather than independent human progress ground truth.
claims.result/denominator: Full2-taskSR95 IR11.1; ablationsSR85–90 IR15.8–18.7, F1 .832–.882; no component uncertainty; counts20/task as overall protocol, no independent ablation repeats.
counterevidence: Proxy progress is successful time/failed zero, so low noise/monotonicity can reflect supervision rather than actual causally necessary progress.
Memory starts already reasonably high while main describes failure-state memory; high-valued retrieval not independently verified feasible.
Risk sigmoid vs separately trained binary head and causal normalization/handback incomplete; high training cosine is not held-out recovery success.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Component removals are consistent with proposed useful monitor/recovery mechanism on2 tasks; does not establish calibrated trigger precision or held-out failure recovery generalization.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Author-reported online physical results on5 trained manipulation tasks showSR88% vs81% and human intervention-step fraction14.6% vs34.3%; two-task ablations support contribution of value trend and memory-goal recovery. Evidence does not establish total human labor, calibrated safety, held-out failure/task generalization or learner-only gains.
unresolved: Evaluation availability of human/recovery stack and exact training/data/time budgets unclear.
Causal runtime value normalization, separate binary/risk-head path and recovery handback insufficiently specified.
No independent reproduction; local source only, original closest-prior papers unavailable.

G.reason: Specific safe-but-unproductive exploration bottleneck versus HiL/failure/reset lineage; broad dominant-human-cost claim and closest-prior originals unverified.

M.reason: Future-value trend plus explicit retrieval goal is reconstructable problem-fit; monotone-time proxy and reachability remain weak assumptions.

X.reason: Most modules/objectives/thresholds and memory construction specified; runtime normalization, binary/risk integration and recovery handback ambiguous, proxy verification not independent.

measurement.reason: Real per-task counts and clear step-basedIR; subjective task tolerance, human-at-test availability, proxy-trigger circularity and candidate-count discrepancy limit trust.

causality.reason: Four leave-out variants and same hardware controls; only2 tasks, larger VLM/data budget vs baseline and learner-vs-recovery contribution not isolated.

holdout.reason: Posttraining eval and proxy validation exist; memory retrieval explicitly training queries, per-task router, no disjoint failure-mode/task coverage or source-data overlap audit.

statistics.reason: 20 eval/task andIR3 runs reported but noIR variance/SR run repeats/CIs or significance; small per-task gains need uncertainty.

cost.reason: Human intervention steps measured, not total attention/reset time; total robot training steps/time, offline data cost and online inference latency absent.

reason: Complete fixed full text and appendices read; provisional calibration-dev judgment. Narrow evidentiary support does not rewrite original broad labor/efficiency claim.
